audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer gave Pantheon all seven stages while the content win[] rows and the packet levelChart both hand Azir the last three. Worse, the full layer's own whys for those three rows describe AZIR winning them ('Emperor's Divide online', 'Nashor's spike: your soldier poke becomes shred', 'Full build Azir is a teamfight') — the row header and the sentence under it said opposite things.
audit.why: Pantheon's kit is front-loaded: Shield Vault 13/12/11/10/9s, Aegis Assault 22s, Grand Starfall 180/165/150s, all short-range. Azir's soldiers plus Emperor's Divide out-range every one of them once items land.
audit.corrected: phases[4..6].side moved to Azir, matching both the content layer and the whys already sitting under them; those whys are also rewritten to name what actually changes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named no cooldown. 'Level 6 adds dive insurance' sat opposite a 180-second ultimate that is the longest cooldown in the matchup and never got mentioned.
audit.why: Grand Starfall: 5500 range, 180/165/150s. Shield Vault falls from 13s to 9s across the lane while Shifting Sands only falls from 22s to 16s — that widening gap is Pantheon's real spike window at 4-5.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text, breakdown.spikes, whys[3..6] and the content mid text rewritten around those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most useful interaction in this matchup was absent: Aegis Assault makes Pantheon invulnerable to damage FROM THE FRONT, which means a Sand Soldier standing in front of him contributes nothing while one placed behind him ignores the shield entirely. The page instead repeated 'point-and-click stun — respect the all-in' four times. Shield Vault's auto-attack reset was also never mentioned.
audit.why: Enemy E text: 'Pantheon sets his shield, becoming invulnerable to damage from the front and striking repeatedly with his spear' — 400 range, 22/21/20/19/18s. Enemy W: 600 range, 13/12/11/10/9s, dash, stun, autoReset flag. Owner R creates terrain, and both Shield Vault and Grand Starfall carry the dash flag, so the wall drops them short.
audit.corrected: Place-the-sand-behind-him now carries tldr, tradeGood, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.early and the content early and late text; the auto reset is stated as the burst tell; wall-versus-dash is stated in breakdown.late and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and dosFull[2].d asserted a 'fifteen-second' Shield Vault — a number that appears nowhere in the kit.
audit.why: Shield Vault is 13/12/11/10/9s. Aegis Assault 22/21/20/19/18s. Grand Starfall 180/165/150s. Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s.
audit.corrected: Wrong number replaced with 13s at rank 1; breakdown.cooldowns now carries three real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] read 'Land Comet Spear stun into a full combo kill'. Comet Spear is not a stun — it is a spear thrust or throw. The stun is Shield Vault.
audit.why: Enemy Q text carries no crowd control and no hardCC flag; the hardCC flag sits on W.
Pantheon is male, so the page's he/his/him usage is right — no pronoun edits made here.

edits.before: Pantheon's spear poke, shield, and stun combo let him dominate trades against your immobile, cooldown-limited kit, making this one of your harder pre-6 lanes. Avoid pushing the wave into his range and never let him get a free stun off — that combo can end lane on the spot. Play maximally passive, farm safely with W, and ask for jungle attention if he starts snowballing.
edits.after: Comet Spear pokes from range and Aegis Assault makes him invulnerable to damage from the front, so a soldier standing ahead of him does nothing — put the sand BEHIND him and drag through. Shield Vault is a 600-range point-and-click stun on 13 seconds that also resets his auto, so the wind-up is your cue to leave, not the cast. Play passive, farm with W, and call jungle if he snowballs.

edits.before: His ultimate lets him disappear and either dive you unexpectedly or swing another lane, so ward for his return and respect the all-in threat even after your own R comes online at 6 — R finally gives you a wall to block his jump-in stun combo. Focus on safe farming and side-wave management rather than direct duels in this stretch, since he still wins isolated fights early. Your scaling is the win condition here, not early trades.
edits.after: Grand Starfall reaches 5500 units on a 180-second cooldown, so when he vanishes, ping it — that absence is another lane's kill. Emperor's Divide is your answer at 6 because it is terrain: Shield Vault is a dash and the Starfall landing is a dash, and a wall drops both short. Farm side waves rather than duelling, and remember Aegis Assault only guards the front, so every soldier you place should sit behind him.

edits.before: Once you have your first item your poke starts punishing his long cooldowns hard, since he has no way to answer at range once you're farmed up, and by two items your zone control and R completely shut down his stun-engage kit — he simply falls off hard past the laning phase. Build early defensive stats (Zhonya's) if he's snowballed a lead, since his combo can still burst you down if unanswered. In teamfights, hold R until he commits his jump, then wall him off from your backline.
edits.after: Nashor's Tooth makes soldier autos hurt, and once his 13-second Shield Vault is spent he has no ranged answer at all — his kit is built for the first ten minutes. By two items your soldiers out-range everything he owns and Emperor's Divide ends both of his dashes. Build Zhonya's if he has snowballed, since the combo still bursts you down. In fights hold R until he commits the vault, then wall him off from your backline and keep the sand behind him where Aegis Assault does not guard.

notes: Pantheon is male, so no pronoun corrections were needed here. Two hard errors fixed: wants.foe[0] called Comet Spear a stun (the stun is Shield Vault), and dosFull[2].d asserted a 'fifteen-second' Shield Vault when the kit says 13/12/11/10/9. The biggest addition is Aegis Assault guarding only the FRONT — Riot's own text — which turns Sand Soldier placement from a generic instruction into a specific one: put the soldier behind him. Level chart disagreed across layers on rows 4, 5 and 6; notably the full layer's own whys for those rows already described Azir winning them while the side said Pantheon, so moving the side to Azir resolves the row against itself as well as against the content layer. NOT asserted: the kit's channel flag claims 'any CC cancels it' for Aegis Assault, which is generic flag boilerplate rather than Riot text — I did not write that Azir's Q slow interrupts the channel, and it is listed in unverified. Ratings left untouched; their semantics are inconsistent across this champion's matchups.
